title: fix(plugin-audit): the compliance ledger keeps no copy of secret-store key material
body:
Part of #26640 — the writer half; the at-rest rewrite's run entry point is #26687.

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：审计台账（`sys_audit_log` 与 `sys_activity`）写入时不再复制密钥存储与两张设置表中的加密密钥材料列；另附一个一次性改写模块，可清除已写入副本中的这些列（热表与归档库）。
- 为什么改：台账是第二份长期留存的副本，此前把应仅限平台访问的加密材料一并复制进去（详情按维护者披露裁决不公开）。
- 风险与回滚：只删副本中的列，不改源表、不改读侧规则；台账仍记录每次创建/更新/删除（哪条记录、标签、密钥 id、算法、版本、操作人与时间）。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/key-material-copy.ts`（规则与名单）、`audit-writers.ts` 中 `ledgerView` 新增的一行调用、`key-material-copy-migration.ts` 的改写器。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-audit exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/audit-internal-field-omission.test.ts src/key-material-copy-migration.test.ts`，预期 2 个文件全部通过。
- 需要你做的：无。已写入旧副本的执行入口（`packages/cli` 的 CLI 命令）由 #26687 承接。

## What changes

- **Writer.** `ledgerView` (the one view every ledger and activity copy is taken through) now omits a closed, writer-held list of key-material columns, by the same disposition as a field declared `internal`: omitted, not masked. The list (`KEY_MATERIAL_COPY_COLUMNS`, `key-material-copy.ts`) names the secret store and the two settings holders, keyed by the platform-object definitions' own names. Neither existing limb reached these columns: they are plain text columns, not credential fields, and not `internal`, because their producers read them back through the generic engine read. `titleFieldOf` refuses a listed column as a record title, as it refuses masked and `internal` columns.
- **What the ledger still records.** Every create, update and delete of those rows keeps its ledger and activity row, with the record id, producer-scoped label, key id, algorithm, version, actor and time. A write that changes only the material still records its row, with the material on neither side. I chose this over excluding the store from the CRUD mirror: the store has three producers, and only the settings producer writes the settings audit trail, so an exclusion would leave the other two with no ledger record at all.
- **The settings holders are in the same class.** Their encrypted-value column holds a handle when a crypto provider is wired and the material inline on the legacy adapter path, and a copy cannot tell which. The holder's own header already says the audit log holds only a placeholder and a digest of an encrypted value. So the copy carries neither (fail closed).
- **Copies already written.** `key-material-copy-migration.ts` adds pure planners (`planKeyMaterialAuditRowPatch`, `planKeyMaterialActivityRowPatch`) and two runners: `migrateKeyMaterialCopies` (engine, hot tables) and `migrateArchivedKeyMaterialCopies` (the archive datasource's driver). They drive the mail-log body rewrite's runner and two stores, which `mail-log-body-migration.ts` now exports as `runLedgerCopyRewrite`, `ledgerCopyStoreOverEngine` and `ledgerCopyStoreOverArchiveDriver`. The mail-log rewrite keeps its behaviour and its log lines. So there is one ledger-copy rewrite, and the write call sites stay the two that already existed: the tenant-audit write-site census is unchanged at 244. Both runs are dry by default and idempotent. They change only the copy column, keep each row's stored `updated_at`, and report counts only. Both runners are exported from the package index.
- **Test config.** `vitest.config.ts` gains one anchored alias for `@objectstack/platform-objects/system`, so the new census resolves the definitions from source (`check:test-source-alias`).
- **Comment.** `sys-secret.object.ts`: the `trackHistory: false` comment now says what the ledger records for the store. Comment only.

## Tests

- `audit-internal-field-omission.test.ts` gains a census block over the REAL definitions. It pins that the writer-held list equals the census and that every listed column is declared by its object, so a rename reds. On create, update and delete, the control column is recorded on every side and no listed column appears on any side or anywhere at rest (ledger or activity). A write of only the material still records its row. A same-named column on an unlisted object is still recorded.
- `key-material-copy-migration.test.ts`: the planners keep every other key, leave unlisted objects and material-free rows alone, and are idempotent. The engine runner covers dry run, apply, re-run as a no-op, writes as the platform keeping `updated_at`, and an unreadable table counted as a failure with no value in any log line. The archive runner runs against a real SQLite driver, including a never-created archive table.

## Acceptance notes

- **Remaining half: the run entry point.** The precedents ship their at-rest rewrite behind an `os migrate …` command in `packages/cli`, which is outside this card's file surface, so this PR ships the exported runners without a command. Copies written before this release keep the material until an entry point runs them: #26687.
- **The mail-log rewrite was restructured, not changed.** Its runner and stores were lifted into exported functions so the key-material rewrite drives the same ones. Its existing test file (`mail-log-body-migration.test.ts`) passes unchanged. The `os migrate audit-mail-bodies` integration tests in `packages/cli` exercise it through the built package and are left to CI.
- **Read side unchanged by design.** The ledger's read rules are not touched.

Ablation (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, the writer's one new call replaced by a no-op, anchor 1 to 0, blob `ad8f76be13d4` to `6ee8dfd95a08`): `Tests 6 failed | 37 passed (43)`. The 6 red are exactly the new census cases (3 objects × 2). Restored: blob equals HEAD (`ad8f76be13d4`), `git diff HEAD` empty. The test imports the writer from source, so no build stood between the mutation and the run.

</details>

<details><summary>Composition check (one-off, not committed)</summary>

A temporary test exercised the real settings producer, its crypto provider and a real `ObjectQL` engine over the real definitions, with the writer installed, through two writes of an encrypted value. On the fix, none of the encrypted values the producer minted was at rest in the ledger, and every create and delete row of the store was still written. With the writer call ablated, every minted value was at rest. No plaintext was at rest in either run. The scratch file was deleted, and nothing of it is committed.

</details>
